subject: History
central_question: How do archaeology, inscriptions, oral traditions and travellers' accounts help reconstruct Vijayanagara's political history, urban design, sacred landscape and everyday life?
in_scope_units: The discovery of Hampi and the combination of historical sources.
Founders, dynasties, rayas, nayakas and Sultanates.
Horse trade, markets and Krishnadeva Raya's reign.
Imperial decline, Talikota and the Aravidu shift.
The capital's natural setting and water resources.
Fortifications, roads, agricultural land and the urban core.
The royal centre, mahanavami dibba and other buildings.
The sacred centre, Virupaksha and Vitthala temples.
Surveying, mapping and unresolved archaeological questions.
banned_topics: Detailed Mughal agrarian society, treated in the next chapter.
The general history of all Deccan Sultanates beyond their relations with Vijayanagara.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Vijayanagara-Sultanate relationship was always religious warfare.
known_pitfalls.correction: Conflict, alliance, support for rival claimants and architectural exchange all occurred across religious boundaries.

known_pitfalls.claim: The royal centre contained only palaces.
known_pitfalls.correction: It included many temples, platforms, halls, water structures and buildings of uncertain function.

known_pitfalls.claim: The surviving ruins provide a complete picture of ordinary life.
known_pitfalls.correction: Stone monuments survive best, while common dwellings and activities must be reconstructed from partial archaeology and travellers' accounts.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 1 on methods of studying Hampi.
NCERT Exercise 6 on the royal centre.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with questions 1-5 in the 100-150 word section, essay questions 6-9, Map work 10 and Projects 11-12.
